AdminDeviceData.description:
One Admin device-list row: spec-approved fields only (16.4, 18.3).

Carries the display identity, the Desktop/Mobile class, the platform, the
validated plugin version, the closed lifecycle status, the
registered/last-seen/revoked moments and the family expiry; never a
credential, hash or polling identity.
AdminDeviceData.title: AdminDeviceData

AdminDeviceListData.description: The Admin device list of one workspace (spec 16.4, 18.3).
AdminDeviceListData.title: AdminDeviceListData

AdminDeviceRevokeData.description: The committed — or already committed — Admin revocation (spec 14.1).
AdminDeviceRevokeData.title: AdminDeviceRevokeData

AdminDeviceRevokeRequest.description: The exact display-name confirmation body of one Admin revoke (14.1).
AdminDeviceRevokeRequest.title: AdminDeviceRevokeRequest

ApiErrorBody.description: The failure body: registry code, safe message, retryability and details.
ApiErrorBody.title: ApiErrorBody

ApiWarning.description:
One non-fatal advisory attached to a response.

The schema is fixed now for contract stability; this child registers no
warning vocabulary and every route returns an empty warning list. Later
children must register public warning codes before using them.
ApiWarning.title: ApiWarning

DeviceAuthorizationGrantState.description:
Closed browser device-authorization grant states (spec 11.4/12, 15.5).

Grant expiry is decided against ``expires_at`` while pending; it is not a
stored state.
DeviceAuthorizationGrantState.title: DeviceAuthorizationGrantState

DeviceGrantContextData.description:
The approval-page display context of one pending grant (spec 11.3).

Carries exactly the values the page must show before any decision: the
same user code the plugin displays, the escaped device name, the platform
class and token, the validated plugin version, the fixed scope and the
expiry. The polling secret never appears.
DeviceGrantContextData.title: DeviceGrantContextData

DeviceGrantData.description:
The one-time provisioning payload of one created grant (spec 11.1).

The user code and polling secret render exactly once here, under the
provisioning cache-suppression headers, and never again.
DeviceGrantData.title: DeviceGrantData

DeviceGrantDecisionData.description: The committed terminal decision of one approve/deny action (11.3).
DeviceGrantDecisionData.title: DeviceGrantDecisionData

DeviceGrantExchangeData.description:
The exchanged device credentials of one grant poll (spec 12.1, 12.2).

The access and refresh credentials render under the provisioning
cache-suppression headers; an exact replay after a lost acknowledgement
re-renders the byte-identical values with the original anchored
timestamps.
DeviceGrantExchangeData.title: DeviceGrantExchangeData

DeviceGrantLookupRequest.description: The user-code body the approval page resolves a grant with (11.2).
DeviceGrantLookupRequest.title: DeviceGrantLookupRequest

DeviceGrantRequest.title: DeviceGrantRequest

DeviceRefreshRequest.description:
The strict rotation body of one refresh presentation (spec 13.4).

``rotation_id`` is the plugin-owned UUID retry identity: one stable
identity replays the exact committed successor, a new identity on a
rotated predecessor is confirmed reuse.
DeviceRefreshRequest.title: DeviceRefreshRequest

DeviceScope.description: The closed fixed Obsidian device scope (spec 6.2).
DeviceScope.title: DeviceScope

DeviceSelfRevokeData.description: The confirmed terminal revoke of one plugin self-revoke (spec 14.2).
DeviceSelfRevokeData.title: DeviceSelfRevokeData

LivenessData.description: Process-liveness success data; it implies no I/O by construction.
LivenessData.title: LivenessData

PasswordChangeRequest.description: The new-password body of one password change (spec 9.5).
PasswordChangeRequest.title: PasswordChangeRequest

ReadinessChecks.description: Canonical dependency check outcomes; this child tracks PostgreSQL only.
ReadinessChecks.title: ReadinessChecks

ReadinessData.description: Readiness success data; failed readiness uses an error envelope instead.
ReadinessData.title: ReadinessData

ReauthenticateRequest.description:
The password body of one recent re-authentication attempt (spec 9.4).

``totp_code`` carries the second factor when the account holds an active
TOTP credential: recent re-auth always verifies the password and also
verifies TOTP when active, so a missing code fails like a wrong one.
ReauthenticateRequest.title: ReauthenticateRequest

RecoveryCodesData.description: One recovery-code revision displayed exactly once (spec 10.3).
RecoveryCodesData.title: RecoveryCodesData

RecoveryLimitedContext.description:
The recovery-limited binding context one accepted recovery produces.

The closed permitted-action set tells the client only TOTP replacement or
logout remains before normal Admin access returns (spec 10.3).
RecoveryLimitedContext.title: RecoveryLimitedContext

RefreshedDeviceTokenData.description:
The successor credentials of one refresh rotation (spec 13.3, 13.4).

The access and refresh credentials render under the provisioning
cache-suppression headers; an exact replay re-renders the byte-identical
successor with its original anchored timestamps and never extends the
family's absolute expiry.
RefreshedDeviceTokenData.title: RefreshedDeviceTokenData

SessionData.description:
The public view of one Web session (spec 9.2).

``state`` covers the closed session-state vocabulary including ``revoked``
(the logout response); ``authenticated`` is true only for an ``active``
session, and the granted scopes stay empty in every non-active state so a
client learns from the login response alone whether a TOTP or recovery
challenge remains before any route authorizes.
SessionData.title: SessionData

TotpCodeRequest.description: The six-digit code body of one TOTP challenge verification.
TotpCodeRequest.title: TotpCodeRequest

TotpEnrollmentAction.description: The strict discriminated enrollment action vocabulary (spec 10.1).
TotpEnrollmentAction.title: TotpEnrollmentAction

TotpEnrollmentData.description:
The response payload of one enrollment action (spec 10.1).

``start`` carries the one-time offer; ``dismiss_initial_offer`` carries
only the recorded dismissal moment — never a secret or pending row.
TotpEnrollmentData.title: TotpEnrollmentData

TotpEnrollmentOfferData.description:
The one-time provisioning material of a started enrollment (10.1).

The provisioning URI and Base32 secret render exactly once, under the
provisioning cache-suppression headers, and never again.
TotpEnrollmentOfferData.title: TotpEnrollmentOfferData

TotpEnrollmentRequest.description: The strict discriminated enrollment action body (spec 10.1).
TotpEnrollmentRequest.title: TotpEnrollmentRequest

TotpProofRequest.description: The shared password plus current TOTP proof body (spec 10.3).
TotpProofRequest.title: TotpProofRequest

TotpRecoveryRequest.description: The password plus one recovery code body (spec 10.3).
TotpRecoveryRequest.title: TotpRecoveryRequest

WebScope.description:
The fixed Phase 2 Web administration scopes (spec 6.1).

A Web session always carries the full surface; the client never chooses,
widens or customizes these values.
WebScope.title: WebScope

RefreshCredential.description: The rt1 refresh credential of one device token family

devicePollingCredential.description: The pg1 polling credential of one device-authorization grant

get.description: List the workspace's plugin devices for the Admin page (18.3).

post.description: Revoke one device behind the full spec 14.1 guard chain.
Create one grant and render the one-time provisioning payload.
Resolve one user code to its approval-page display context.
Approve one grant behind the recent-authentication gate (11.3).
Deny one grant: explicit, terminal, no recent window (spec 11.3).

Poll one grant with its polling credential (spec 11.4, 12).

The polling Bearer credential in the dedicated scheme is the only
authority: session cookies and every other credential are never
read. A pending grant answers the closed pending outcome with the
five-second hint, a too-fast poll the slow-down outcome, and an
approved grant exchanges once — an exchanged grant replays the exact
committed credentials while the initial generation stays current.

Rotate the current refresh credential or replay the successor (13.4).

The refresh Bearer credential in its dedicated scheme is the only
authority: session cookies, polling credentials and access
credentials close with the registered invalid-credential code. The
presented rotation identity is the plugin-owned retry identity — one
stable identity replays the byte-identical committed successor, a new
identity on a rotated predecessor commits the confirmed-reuse
revocation and surfaces the terminal reuse code.

Self-revoke the family of the presented refresh credential (14.2).

The current refresh credential authenticates the disconnect: one
locked transaction revokes its family and every usable token, and
the confirmed response tells the plugin to overwrite its local
credential record with the non-secret tombstone. Spec 14.2 names no
request body — the credential itself is the whole authority.
Run one password login and issue the session and CSRF bindings.

Revoke the session row, then clear both browser cookies.

Spec 9.2 reaches logout from every unrevoked state — a pending or
recovery-limited session logs out too — so the dependency tolerates
those states while the CSRF triple check stays identical.

put.description: Change the password, revoke other sessions and rotate this one.

post.description: Verify the password — and TOTP when active — then rotate (spec 9.4).

get.description: Return the authenticated session view of the presented binding.

delete.description: Close every TOTP surface and rotate to password-only (spec 10.3).

post.description: Verify one enrollment code, activate and return the codes once.
Consume one recovery code and enter the recovery-limited state.
Re-verify password plus current TOTP and issue a fresh code set.
Verify one login TOTP challenge and activate the pending binding.

get.description: Report process liveness: a constant payload, no dependency consulted.
